newsitem.title: USA: Viacom sees Internet revenue potential.
newsitem.headline: Viacom sees Internet revenue potential.

text.p: Viacom Inc's Blockbuster Entertainment Group said Thursday it sees various revenue possibilities with little risk in its Internet access deal with Sprint Corp.
The companies said earlier Thursday they would offer an Internet access package via Blockbuster's 3,200 music and video stores across the United States.
The deal combines Sprint's Internet access product with software focused on entertainment. The software is free, but users are required to pay Sprint a monthly access fee.

Tom Byrne, vice chairman of Blockbuster, said in an interview that the company would take advantage of marketing tools already in place, for example point of purchase marketing at the stores, advertising on in-store television monitors and inserts in Blockbuster direct mail campaigns.
"We're really using all of our marketing opportunities to get the word out to our subscribers," Byrne said, adding there was little cost involved.

With the software, users are given initial access to a Blockbuster site on the Internet. From there, users will eventually be able to enter cyberstores to test and buy music, videos, books and software, Byrne said. There are also bookmarks connecting the user to other entertainment-related Internet sites.
"As each of these individual stores come up, there is (sales) transaction volume," Byrne said.
Byrne declined to project the revenue potential for Blockbuster, but said there were many possibilities.
"As part of our deal with Sprint we get a one-time bounty" as well as a portion of the income stream, Byrne said.

Blockbuster will also sell advertising on its Internet sites to other concerns, and the package is good advertising for Blockbuster itself, Byrne said. Each time a user logs on he will be reminded of Blockbuster.
Sprint and Blockbuster plan initially to hand out 1.5 million disks to users.
